content: The release date of the first edition of the Model Aquatic Health Code (MAHC) aligns with the NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013, which is the current applicable standard for precoated filters. Filters previously referred to as diatomaceous earth filters have been renamed precoated filters due to the significant use of alternative filter media, such as perlite. At the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release, NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013 is the applicable standard for filter media. For cartridge filters, the NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013 is also the applicable standard as of the release date of the MAHC 1st Edition. Regarding other filter types, the NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013 remains the applicable standard at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release. For mechanical chemical feeding equipment, the applicable standards as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date are NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013, UL 1081, and CSA C22. For ozone generators, the applicable standards at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release include NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013, UL 1081, CSA C22, and the United States National Electrical Code NFPA-70 (2008). For ultraviolet light systems, the applicable standards as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date are NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013 (which includes testing for Cryptosporidium validation), CSA C22, and the United States National Electrical Code NFPA-70 (2008). For in-line electrolytic chlorinators, the applicable standards at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release include NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013, UL 1081, CSA C22, the United States National Electrical Code NFPA-70 (2008), and the Canadian PMRA. For brine batch electrolytic chlorine or bromine generators, the applicable standards as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date are NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013, UL 1081, CSA C22, the United States National Electrical Code NFPA-70 (2008), and the Canadian PMRA. For copper/silver and copper ion generators, the applicable standards at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release include NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013, UL 1081, CSA C22, the United States National Electrical Code NFPA-70 (2008), and the Canadian PMRA. For chemical storage, the applicable standard as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date is the United States National Fire Code NFPA-1 (2009). For automated controllers, the applicable standards at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release include NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013 and the United States National Electrical Code NFPA-70 (2008). For water quality testing devices, the applicable standard as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date is NSF/ANSI Standard 50-2013. For general electrical equipment, the applicable standard at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release is the United States National Electrical Code NFPA-70 (2008). For lights, the applicable standards as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date include UL 1241 (Junction Boxes for Swimming Pool Luminaires), UL 676 (Underwater Luminaires and Submersible Junction Boxes), UL 8750 (Light Emitting Diode Equipment for Use in Lighting Products), and UL 379 (Transformers for Fountain, Swimming Pool, and Spa Luminaires). For diving boards and platforms, the applicable standard at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release is ANSI/NSPI-1 2003. For starting blocks, the applicable standards as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date include ANSI/NSPI-1 2003, FINA, NFSHSA, and NCAA. For lifeguard chairs, the applicable standard at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release is ANSI/NSPI-1 2003. For ladders, the applicable standard as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date is ANSI/NSPI-1 2003. For handrails, the applicable standard at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release is ANSI/NSPI-1 2003. For stairs, the applicable standard as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date is ANSI/NSPI-1 2003. For handicapped lifts, the applicable standard at the time of the MAHC 1st Edition release is the Americans with Disabilities Act, which is regulated by the Department of Justice. For safety covers, the applicable standards as of the MAHC 1st Edition release date include ANSI/NSPI-1 2003, ASTM 1346, and UL 2452.
